hs_sd_4ec: HE3AT is an exciting, place-based, post-secondary preparation program designed to provide students with an augmented learning opportunity to explore social, political, technological and economic complexities in the fields of healthcare, energy, education, environment, agriculture and technology. Curriculum is intentionally designed to connect work- and place-based experiences with academic and project management skills to better prepare students for careers, occupations, and credentials of their interest. Students have access to a wide variety of industry specific reading material calibrated to their interest as they build and develop their literacy skills and interest in reading towards increasingly complex texts. Sustained partnerships with industry leaders in private and public sectors provide students with authentic learning that combines academics with in-demand professional skills. Once a month, from 8:30am-2:30 pm, students travel to their assigned place-based learning locations at one of our partner sites where they collaborate with industry experts, NYCPS teachers and students from other schools. Industry professionals facilitate interactive learning experiences where students engage with principles of design thinking, applied entrepreneurship and ethical business management in addressing pressing issues that lack rules-based solutions with a lens of empathy, equity, social justice, and sustainability. Instead of seeking solutions that totally eliminate problems, students learn to recognize that actions occur in an ongoing process, and further actions will always be needed. Students' experience culminates in extensive research and a development of a relevant, industry-specific proposal, prototype design, or a business plan along with an oral defense to a panel on their research process, method, and findings. Students earn two credits and acquire financial literacy skills as they get paid for their place-based experience. We also offer excellent Academic Place-based Learning & Civic Readiness course starting spring 2024. The opportunity is dedicated to engaging students profoundly with the history of the Freedom Riders while anchored in the moral compass of kindness, embracing the values of forgiveness, compassion, integrity, and responsibility.
